criterion_notes.c1: Discusses basic sanitation (water supply and sewage/sanitation services under Law 11.445/2007) and persistent deficits in household sanitation coverage in Brazil, particularly in smaller municipalities.
criterion_notes.c2: Passes the plain wording of Criterion 2 (plain=yes) because it discusses legal, institutional, and governance arrangements in Brazilian federalism (Art. 23 CF/88, Law 11.445/2007, Law 11.107/2005, Bill 4.162/2019, intergovernmental coordination, and fiscal constraints). Fails the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading (narrow=no) because it focuses on macro-governance background—federalist decentralization, horizontal/vertical fragmentation across federal ministries, municipal planning/technical capacity deficits, and macro-fiscal budget trends—rather than analyzing a specific rule-type mechanism directly governing household or community service access. Note that even under the plain wording of Criterion 2, the paper is still excluded due to lack of empirical evidence (Criterion 3).
criterion_notes.c3: Non-empirical policy/institutional essay based on a narrative literature review, legislation review, and illustrative descriptive charts drawn from secondary government databases (SNIS, SIGA Brasil, SIOP) without an empirical research design, primary data collection, empirical analysis, or systematic synthesis. Excluded under E05.
criterion_notes.c4: Does not report an empirically analyzed service-access outcome; only cites one background descriptive chart from SNIS (2017) on state-level percentage of households with treated sewage alongside descriptive charts on municipal planning instruments, federal agency counts, and federal budget execution.
criterion_notes.c5: No identifiable empirical study design, sample, or analyzed exposure-outcome relationship; narrative policy essay and non-systematic literature review.
criterion_notes.c6: Published in Portuguese, which is directly eligible without translation under Criterion 9.

raw_response.exposure: Brazilian federalist institutional arrangement, decentralization, fragmentation of federal sanitation programs, and national sanitation legal framework (Law 11.445/2007 and Bill 4.162/2019)
raw_response.outcome: No empirically analyzed access outcome (cites background state-level household treated-sewage coverage from SNIS 2017 alongside municipal planning instruments and federal budget execution)
raw_response.population_and_sample: Brazilian Federation (federal agencies and municipalities discussed at a macro-policy level; no empirical study sample)
raw_response.rationale: Excluded under E05 (No empirical evidence). This Portuguese-language article is a narrative literature review and macro-level policy/institutional essay examining challenges of Brazilian federalism, intergovernmental coordination, municipal technical/fiscal capacity deficits, and federal institutional fragmentation in basic sanitation, concluding with six normative policy recommendations. Although it cites four illustrative descriptive charts from government databases (SNIS 2017 state-level sewage coverage and municipal management instruments, SIGA Brasil federal agency counts, and SIOP 2015-2019 federal budget execution), it has no empirical methodology, no primary data, no systematic synthesis, and no empirical analysis linking a rule-type legal/administrative mechanism to a household or community service-access outcome. It also fails the narrow 2026-10-13 Criterion 2 reading because it addresses macro-governance federalism background rather than a specific rule-type access mechanism, and would likewise be excluded under the plain Criterion 2 wording for lack of empirical evidence.
raw_response.study_design: Narrative literature review and policy/institutional essay (non-empirical)
